text:
sam: FYI I'm digging into a peering failover incident where tenant tunnel keepalives trigger a burst of UDP probes and we lose SNAT ephemeral ports for ~1-2s, causing upstream 502s.

cheng: can you paste repro?

sam: repro: 1) simulate cp-eu1 outage -> control-plane peering flips 2) tenant agent uses UDP keepalives every 3s 3) agent reprobes during rebind, kernels allocate new ephemeral ports -> conntrack entries evicted 4) short window where packets drop.

maria: saw a similar blip in logs for a Dedicated customer. conntrack shows mass TIME_WAIT/DELETE around the failover. devops-bot: archived flow logs at s3://redwood-debug/peering-races/7901234567.tar.gz

alan: root cause seems twofold: (A) synchronized aggressive keepalives from agents; (B) short conntrack lifetimes + SNAT pool remapping when outbound path changes.

jess: idea: force keepalive probe pinning to the original source address/port pair while a peering-change flag is active. That avoids creating new SNAT tuples mid-failover.

cheng: probe pinning helps, but requires the agent to remember the 5-tuple and re-send from same socket during the transient. Some kernels will still rotate if socket closed.

sam: practical proposal: three layers: short-term = staggered default keepalive + client jitter (5s +/- jitter) medium = agent-side probe backoff on consecutive failures (exp backoff after N failures) medium-plus = conntrack short-hold on flows with cp-failover label long-term = dedicated management-plane probe path for control-plane health checks (no SNAT).

maria: metrics request: emit cp.peering.keepalive.backoffs, cp.conntrack.hold_hits, and cp.probe.stale_port_count. Add dashboard and an alert on conntrack eviction spikes.

alan: about conntrack hold: we can tag flows during an observed peering rebind (set connmark) and extend timeout to, say, 8s. Tradeoffs: memory pressure and risk of routing to a dead egress if the peer is actually unreachable.

jess: maybe make the conntrack hold conservative: only extend for flows with recent activity (last 30s) and cap total held entries per customer. Also pair with a liveness probe - if peer doesn't respond, flush rather than hold.

cheng: another option: let the edge do SNAT pool affinity by session cookie of the agent. That way when CP flips, we prefer to reassign the same SNAT range to the new relay for a short window. More service-level complexity.

sam: rollout plan suggestion: 1) change agent default keepalive -> 5s ± jitter, rollout in agent 2) implement probe backoff behind feature flag, enable for Private + Dedicated canaries 3) instrument metrics and run chaos test that rebinds peering while varying jitter 4) prototype conntrack-hold as RFC appendix if backoff doesn't resolve.

maria: I can own metrics + dashboard. I'll create panels for conntrack evictions, backoff counts, and probe burst histograms.

alan: I'll draft the conntrack-hold appendix with memory budgeting and edge cases (stale route detection). Include nfctool/iptables snippets and a flush rollback runbook.

cheng: I'll add a cron chaos job `peering-probe-rebind` in cp-peering repo to exercise agent jitter/backoff combinations. Tag it in CI so canary runs nightly.

sam: decision for now: implement agent jitter + backoff as soft mitigation, add metrics, and run chaos. Holding conntrack is a lower-priority prototype. Long-term opt-in management-plane probes for Dedicated customers remains on the table.

devops-bot: created ticket #1402 "agent-probe-backoff-and-metrics" assigned alan, maria, cheng

maria: scheduling 30m sync once alan posts RFC appendix draft.

sam: thanks team. please add short notes to the RFC followup doc and link any prototypes. We'll avoid sweeping keepalive reductions globally; prefer targeted backoff + observability.
